user.title: Add a webcam
user.description: Point this at a URL that returns a single still image. Home Assistant fetches it on a schedule and keeps the frames so you can scrub back through them.

data_description.url: The direct link to the image itself, not the page it sits on. It usually ends in .jpg or .png.
data_description.capture_interval: How often to save a frame. Shorter intervals use more disk and put more load on the camera's server.
data_description.retention_days: Older frames are deleted automatically. At 10 minutes and 1024 px, one day is roughly 10 MB.

data_description.max_width: Frames are scaled down to this width. Images already narrower are left alone.
data_description.quality: Higher keeps more detail and uses more disk.
data_description.live_refresh: How often the camera entity fetches a fresh image. Set to 0 to only ever show the last captured frame.
data_description.frames_path: Leave empty to store frames inside Home Assistant's config folder, where backups skip them.
data_description.username: Only needed if the camera is behind HTTP basic authentication.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure webcam
reconfigure.description: Change any setting without losing the frames already captured.

reauth_confirm.title: Camera credentials needed
reauth_confirm.description: {url} refused the last request. Enter the credentials to use from now on.

error.cannot_connect: Could not reach that URL. Check the address, and that Home Assistant can see the camera.
error.invalid_url: That does not look like a complete URL.
error.invalid_scheme: Only http:// and https:// addresses are supported.
error.invalid_interval: Choose one of the listed capture intervals.
error.not_an_image: That URL returned a page, not an image. Use the direct link to the image file.
error.timeout: The camera did not respond in time.

abort.already_configured: This image URL is already set up.
abort.unique_id_mismatch: That URL belongs to a different camera than the one you are reconfiguring.

data_description.retention_days: Lowering this deletes older frames on the next capture. They cannot be recovered.

error.cannot_connect: Could not reach that URL. Check the address, and that Home Assistant can see the camera.
error.invalid_url: That does not look like a complete URL.
error.invalid_scheme: Only http:// and https:// addresses are supported.
error.invalid_interval: Choose one of the listed capture intervals.
error.not_an_image: That URL returned a page, not an image. Use the direct link to the image file.
error.timeout: The camera did not respond in time.

capture_now.name: Capture now
capture_now.description: Saves a frame straight away instead of waiting for the next scheduled capture.

entry_id.name: Camera
entry_id.description: Which configured webcam to capture from.

purge_frames.name: Delete all frames
purge_frames.description: Permanently deletes every stored frame for this camera. The timelapse starts over from the next capture.

pause_capture.name: Pause capturing
pause_capture.description: Stops saving frames until capturing is resumed. Frames already stored are kept.

resume_capture.name: Resume capturing
resume_capture.description: Starts saving frames again on the usual schedule.

export_video.name: Export video
export_video.description: Renders a stretch of the stored frames into an MP4 in the media folder. Finishes once the video is written, which can take a few minutes.

entry_id.name: Camera
entry_id.description: Which configured webcam to export from.

start.name: From
start.description: First moment to include. Leave empty to start at the oldest stored frame.

end.name: To
end.description: Last moment to include. Leave empty to end at the newest stored frame.

fps.name: Frames per second
fps.description: Playback rate of the video. At 24, one day captured every 5 minutes plays in 12 seconds.

max_width.name: Maximum width
max_width.description: Scale the video down to this width. 0 keeps the size of the stored frames.

deflicker.name: Smooth brightness
deflicker.description: Evens out cloud-driven brightness jumps, like the card does during playback. 0 turns it off.

timestamp.name: Show date and time
timestamp.description: Stamps each frame with the moment it was captured.

timestamp_size.name: Date and time size
timestamp_size.description: Width of the date and time, as a percentage of the video's width.

overlay.name: Sensor readings
overlay.description: Readings to draw on the video, in the same form as the card's configuration: entities, entities_left, overlay_title, overlay_title_left, graph_hours, show_graph and show_sun.

readings_size.name: Sensor readings size
readings_size.description: Width of the readings block, as a percentage of the video's width. With two blocks, this is the wider one.

readings_position.name: Readings position
readings_position.description: Where the card's readings block (its entities) goes. Left and right are the bottom corners, as on the card; top and bottom centre it on that edge. Leave empty to keep the card's place.

readings_position_left.name: Left readings position
readings_position_left.description: The same for the card's second block (entities_left).

camera_offline.title: {entry_title} has stopped sending new images
camera_offline.description:
The last {ticks} captures returned exactly the same image, which usually means the camera, or the software feeding it, has stopped. Frames are not being saved until it recovers, so the timelapse will show a gap for this period.

Check that the camera is powered on and that its image URL still opens in a browser.
